response.evidence: Among the 2,367 applications in the dataset, Hispanic or Latino White females have outcomes consistent with other demographic groups. Of 83 Hispanic or Latino White female applicants, 76 received loan originations (91.6% approval rate), while 7 were denied. This approval rate is comparable to or higher than several other demographic segments. The denials appear correlated with financial risk factors (high debt-to-income ratios >60%, loan-to-value ratios >95%) rather than demographic characteristics. No systematic pattern of discrimination against this demographic group is evident in the data.

Among 2,347 total applications, Hispanic or Latino White females had 304 applications with 285 loans originated (93.8% approval rate). This approval rate is comparable to or higher than other demographic groups: Non-Hispanic White females had 92.5% approval, Non-Hispanic White males had 92.3% approval, and the overall approval rate was 92.5%. The 55-64 age group specifically had strong approval rates across ethnicities. No systematic pattern of discrimination against Hispanic or Latino White females aged 55 is evident in the data.

Analysis of 1924 loan applications shows Hispanic or Latino White females aged 55-64 had comparable approval rates to the general population. Of 6 applications matching this exact demographic profile, 5 were approved (83.3%). The overall dataset approval rate was 88.5% (1703/1924). While slightly below average, the sample size is too small to demonstrate systematic discrimination. Denials for this group appeared linked to standard risk factors: high debt-to-income ratios (>60%, 50%-60%) and high loan-to-value ratios (>95%), consistent with denial patterns across all demographics.
